chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not make anything from the deeds of the children of Adam more honored to Him than the Hajj and 'Umrah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the most honored act of worship in Islam according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq situates this hadith within the broader theological framework of Shia jurisprudence, where Hajj and 'Umrah are not merely ritualistic obligations but supreme acts of devotion that purify the soul and affirm submission to the Divine Will. This elevation of status underscores their role as foundational pillars of faith, distinguishing them from other acts of worship by their unique capacity to unite the believer with the universal call of Allah.
